LESSON: COOKING FOOD • GRILLING • ROASTING • STEAMING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.4: Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming, part of Food Production Processes in Grade 7 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use different methods of cooking food?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe methods of cooking different types of foods

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. cook food using various methods

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of varied methods of cooking food. Learners are guided to: • use digital resources, print materials, or resource persons to source for information on grilling, roasting, and steaming foods • practise grilling, steaming, and roasting methods to prepare foods while observing the safety of self and others. • serve grilled, steamed, and roasted foods to appreciate the various methods of cooking. Why should we use different methods of cooking food?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe methods of cooking different types of foods

   Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. cook food using various methods

   Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the use of varied methods of cooking food. Learners are guided to: • use digital resources, print materials, or resource persons to source for information on grilling, roasting, and steaming foods • practise grilling, steaming, and roasting methods to prepare foods while observing the safety of self and others. • serve grilled, steamed, and roasted foods to appreciate the various methods of cooking. Why should we use different methods of cooking food?

   Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Cooking Food • Grilling • Roasting • Steaming together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Responsibility: taking care of cooking equipment as learners engage in steaming and roasting methods.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety of self and others as learners use sharp tools and fuels in cooking.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners relate cooking methods to the transfer of heat learnt in Integrated Science.
